title: Glasshouse and Inventory
premise: Wren Vane, a celebrated restaurant critic who lost his sense of taste after the fire that killed his mother, has built a career on elegant evasion. When the glasshouse where she grew her heirloom tomatoes goes up for auction, Wren discovers his estranged half-sister Marisol has been quietly squatting in it, tending the garden and caring for their dying grandfather — a man who allegedly forged the will that disinherited them both. As Wren investigates the forgery, he must choose between publishing the exposé that would save the house and destroy the found family of neighbors who sheltered his grandfather's secret. In the end, Wren trades his byline for testimony, the auction is voided, and tasting a tomato from the restored glasshouse, he finally grieves — and belongs.
about_author: E. M. Vasquez is the pen name of a former line cook turned literary novelist who grew up above a family restaurant in the Central Valley. Their work explores inheritance, appetite, and the families we assemble one meal at a time.

chapters.title: The Palate of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At a Michelin-starred tasting menu, Wren writes another luminous review describing flavors he cannot taste, hiding his condition even from his editor. A letter arrives: the Hollis glasshouse estate is entering probate auction. Emotional beat: polished loneliness cracked open by the past.

chapters.title: Lot 47
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. He researches the auction catalog and finds photographs of the glasshouse still standing — and a figure moving inside it in recent images. His lawyer warns him the estate is entangled in a contested will. Emotional beat: curiosity sharpening into dread.

chapters.title: The Road Back to Hollis
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. He drives to his hometown for the pre-auction viewing, passing the diner where his mother once worked. The town remembers him as the boy who left after the fire. Emotional beat: shame meeting nostalgia.

chapters.title: Marisol
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Marisol Vane, who has lived secretly in the glasshouse cottage for two years, nursing their grandfather Aurelio and reviving his seed collection. She recognizes Wren at the viewing and says nothing. Emotional beat: guarded hope.

chapters.title: What the Appraiser Missed
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. During the open house, Wren finds his mother's handwriting in a seed ledger dated after the fire — proof someone survived longer than he was told. Emotional beat: vertigo of discovered lies.

chapters.title: Aurelio's Silence
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. She introduces Wren to Aurelio, who has aphasia after a stroke but grips Wren's wrist and weeps. Marisol explains the will left everything to a church charity no one can locate. Emotional beat: fragile truce between siblings.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Almost
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, flashback chapter. Reconstructing the fire, the funeral he fled, and how his taste died with his mother. He realizes his reviews have been elegies all along. Emotional beat: grief acknowledged at last.

chapters.title: The Neighbors' Table
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Marisol brings Wren to a Sunday supper hosted by the Delgado family, who fed Aurelio through his decline. Wren tastes nothing but is moved anyway. Emotional beat: first warmth of found family.

chapters.title: Paper Trail
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. With a retired notary's help, he confirms the signature on the will was traced — but the evidence points ambiguously toward Aurelio himself. Emotional beat: suspicion turning inward.

chapters.title: The Church That Isn't
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The siblings trace the beneficiary charity to a shell entity connected to a local developer, Dale Pruitt, who has been buying up Hollis farmland. Emotional beat: righteous anger.

chapters.title: Deadline at the County Clerk
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Objections to the auction must be filed in nine days; Wren's editor offers a front-page slot if he delivers the story fast. Emotional beat: ambition colliding with loyalty.

chapters.title: Seeds in a Coffee Can
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Aurelio, in a lucid hour, presses a coffee can of seeds into Wren's hands and scrawls 'she knew.' They realize their mother may have known about the original theft of the land. Emotional beat: inherited burden.

chapters.title: Pruitt Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Pruitt offers Wren money to bury the story and Marisol cash to leave quietly. Wren almost accepts — his career is starving. Emotional beat: temptation at its most human.

chapters.title: The Fight in the Glasshouse
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Marisol discovers Wren met Pruitt; a furious argument erupts among the tomato vines about who abandoned whom twelve years ago. Old wounds bleed. Emotional beat: rupture before repair.

chapters.title: Dolores Delgado's Testimony
chapters.summary: Dolores Delgado's POV. She reveals Aurelio confessed to signing the forged will — under threat that Pruitt would report Marisol's unpaid caregiving debts and evict them both. Emotional beat: compassion reframing guilt.

chapters.title: What Justice Costs
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Filing the objection means exposing Aurelio's coerced signature publicly, humiliating a dying man. Wren drafts two versions of the story: the exposé and the truth. Emotional beat: moral crucible.

chapters.title: The Auction
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Bidding opens as Wren stands to speak; Pruitt's attorney moves to strike him. Marisol rises beside him, then the whole Delgado table. Emotional beat: solidarity made visible.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, climax. Before the judge, Wren reads the seed ledger aloud — his mother's own words about the stolen land — and withdraws his byline, submitting instead sworn statements from Dolores and the notary. Emotional beat: sacrifice of self for truth.

chapters.title: Voided
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The sale is voided pending investigation into Pruitt's shell charity; Aurelio, hearing the ruling, speaks his first full sentence in months: 'Home.' Emotional beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: First Taste
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Weeks later, in the replanted glasshouse, Wren bites a sun-warmed tomato grown from his mother's seeds — and tastes it. He weeps over something so small. Emotional beat: restoration of the senses.

chapters.title: Inventory
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The siblings inventory the estate together: what to keep, what to give away, what to plant. Wren resigns from criticism to write a book about the town's food and its people. Emotional beat: choosing presence over performance.

chapters.title: Glasshouse, Lit
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV, closing chapter. On the first anniversary supper held in the restored glasshouse, neighbors, the Delgados, and a recovering Aurelio gather under lit glass while Wren sets the table. Final line: he writes down what everything tastes like. Emotional beat: belonging, earned.
